speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The bar's down across the street door. She'll have no light in the front of the house, lest a lit pane draw a stone. I have the one candle on the boards behind the bed, and my hand round it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A thousand of them on Tower Hill, the boy cried, running through the close. And some of the Tower's own warders with them. A thousand. I can't see one of them. I can only hear them.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It comes and goes like a sea. …There. And now nothing. And now there.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Friday they set a gallows at the Mayor's own gate. A hundred yards from this bed. All for fivepenny butter and a loaf a man could hide in his fist.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Verbeke went up into the garret without a word said to him. He knows what a crowd says to a stranger. He knew it before I did.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: …If they come up Bishopsgate they come for him, not us. They'd pass this door. They'd pass it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: My heart goes like a fuller's mill. Ridiculous. I am in my own chamber with the bar down.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Remember this dark. When I come to the two houses, begin there. Not in a palace. In the street, among the serving-men, with the heat on them and one word too many.
